correctness.rationale: For every tree n≥2, LL†=L†L=I−11^T/n gives barycentric facet map lambda_i(x)=1/n+<L†e_i,x>, whose unit normalized facets have clearance lambda_i/||L†e_i||. Summing clearances yields inradius rho=1/S and the unique barycentrically weighted center. For the all-tree lower radius bound, Cauchy and Σmu^-2≤(Σmu^-1)^2 bound S≤sqrt(n)tr L†=W(T)/sqrt(n), and the tree leaf-distance inductive bound W≤n(n²−1)/6 yields rho≥6/[sqrt(n)(n²−1)]. For upper radius bound at least (n+2)/2 vertices have degree≤2 and each has a neighboring branch size≥(n−1)/2; the pseudoinverse Poisson equation gives adjacent potential jump b/n and norm≥b/(sqrt(2)n); summing obtains S≥(n+2)(n−1)/(4sqrt(2)n). Exact path potentials/norm quartic independently checked for every 2≤n≤45 and vertex and star KKT/norm algebra checked. Riemann-sum limit gives path n^-5/2, star n^-1. No fixed-n exact extremal ordering claimed.
residual_risks: Existing literature independently derives star/path pseudoinverse matrices; the new result is the canonical simplex metric plus uniform tree bounds, not novelty of those matrices.
Only finite simple unweighted trees and canonical full-zero-sum embedding; not arbitrary lattice coordinate transforms or exact extremizing trees for fixed n.
